items.scene: Two roommates want the only quiet study room on Saturday. One has an online exam from 9 to 12. The other wants the room all day to finish a presentation.
items.question: What is the best plan?
options: Give the room to the exam-taker from 9 to 12, then let the other roommate use it afterward.
Tell the exam-taker to study elsewhere so the presentation gets the room all day.
Split the day exactly in half, even though the exam has a fixed start time.
Ignore both requests and choose whoever asked first.
items.why_this_case_matters: Direct compromise with fixed and flexible needs; both sides adjust around a shared plan.

items.scene: A supervisor tells an employee, 'The report must be in by Friday.' The employee says they are confused about one requirement in the template.
items.question: What should happen next?
options: Negotiate a new deadline and trade tasks between them.
Clarify the template requirement first, since the issue is understanding the instruction.
Offer a compromise where each side gives up part of the deadline.
Ask the employee to persuade the supervisor to change the deadline.
items.why_this_case_matters: This is mostly clarification, not a mutual-adjustment bargaining scene.

items.scene: A neighbor accidentally breaks another neighbor's lamp during a move. The owner is upset and asks what should be said next.
items.question: What is the best response?
options: Apologize and offer to replace or pay for the lamp.
Try to negotiate a long-term shared plan for future moving days.
Explain that both sides should compromise equally on the damage.
Ask the owner to forget it without any repair.
items.why_this_case_matters: The main task is apology and repair, not bargaining over a joint future plan.

items.scene: Two coworkers both want Friday off. One has a family event that cannot move. The other wants a long weekend and is flexible about which Friday they take.
items.question: Which agreement best fits the situation?
options: Give both people Friday off and leave the team short-staffed.
Make them split the day evenly, even though one need is fixed all day.
Deny both requests because only one person can ever be absent.
Let the person with the family event take this Friday, and offer the other coworker a different Friday or shift swap.
items.why_this_case_matters: Tests the common wrong shortcut of equal splitting when one side has a fixed constraint and the other is flexible.
